question: Why did UK unemployment rise in 2009?
summary: UK unemployment rose in 2009: 6.5% (2008-12) -> 7.9% (2009-06 peak), +1.4 pts; 2007 average 5.3%. The evidence is consistent with one driver: UK industrial production fell during the run-up to the 2009 peak. Only one independent driver was supported, so treat this as a partial explanation.
supported: UK industrial production fell during the run-up to the 2009 peak

H1: UK industrial production fell during the run-up to the 2009 peak
H2: UK short-term interest rates rose during the run-up to the 2009 peak
H3: The 12-month change in Brent crude oil prices rose during the run-up to the 2009 peak

reference: Unemployment rose to about 8% during the 2008-09 recession that followed the global financial crisis, as output fell (ONS labour market statistics; GDP fell about 4% in 2009).
